chapter: Bebop, Tadd Dameron, Slam Stewart and Europe
title: How music changed with bebop; meeting Sarah Vaughan
summary: Postwar music had fast, changing tempos and was for listening, not dancing; Collins felt at home, and Dameron introduced him to Sarah Vaughan.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Oh, everything that had happened. It was no -- I mean, it was all bebop. Now, the whole structure of music had changed, and here's Dizzy again. Dizzy and Bird, the tempos were super-fast, like before when I went into the army people would dance. Nobody danced any more now, they -- everything was a concert. The music, the tempos -- there was not a dancing tempo. You had to listen because the tempo would change, you'd go from three/four to four/four to seven/four and everything was a concert.

So it was freer, it was beautiful, you know. It was like someone had broken out of a cage and everybody -- you know, everybody was free now to explore different areas of -- the world was new. And it was just invigorating, it was just exciting, you know.
Did you get any new ideas?

Oh, yes. Well, actually I had been kind of doing it any way, you know, but I had been doing it just for musicians. You know, I would play for Dizzy or I would play for Benny or I would play for some of these guys, not in public. We'd just sit down and play. But I never did do it in public. Now it's being done in public, and so it was like, what do you say, throwing a rabbit in a briar patch for me. It put me right in my element now. And it was just

beautiful.
Now, I could really go and study and practice and do the things that I wanted to do, you know. So one of the nights I was up there Tad said, look, John, come -- this was in the Braddock Hotel. Tad was living there, and he said come on up to my room, I have someone I want you to meet. So I knocked on the door and I went in there, and they introduced me to Sarah Vaughan. I hadn't -- I had heard her but I hadn't met her. Just thrilled. So he was writing this thing, she was going to do a recording date with him, and he was writing this tune, 'If You Could See Me Now'. It was a beautiful thing, which they made a tremendous record.
